_comment: Data of the 23 walk cases (t-2006 sec 1-2). Text comes from each card's steps-by-hand and expected-with-source fields only (R1); the cards' seen/who/status fields and SUMMARY.md are never copied here. {LOGIN:<actor>} expands to the sign-in sentence of worked example C. Ids: LOCAL-1_TC_1NN, NN = card number.

cases.title: Book page - quantity 0, -1, 1.5 and text
cases.given: A guest session. The book "1984"; read its stock on its page first.
steps: Open the book page of "1984".
Select the whole quantity field, key 0 one character at a time, click Add to Cart.
Read the field, the message on the page and the cart badge; open /cart and read the lines. Empty the cart again.
Do the last two steps for -1, then 1.5, then abc (paste the value if the field does not take the keys).

thens.text: Quantity 0 is rejected with a clear message and nothing is added to the cart.
thens.ref: Jira XPANBFLFA-140

thens.text: -1, 1.5 and abc are each rejected the same way and nothing is added to the cart.
thens.ref: owner, gate A 02.11: R-8 a, R-9 a, R-10 a, Q1 a (reject)

row.what: quantity 0, -1, 1.5, text on the book page
row.behavior: the book page refuses a bad quantity with a message and adds nothing
row.boundary: live stand: field, message, badge, cart lines
row.completion: each value keyed and its result recorded

cases.dropped: Card step 5 (a POST /api/cart control call expecting 400): the step vocabulary has no POST (F4).

cases.title: Book page - clearing and re-keying the quantity field
cases.given: A guest session. The book "1984".
steps: Open the book page of "1984".
Select the whole quantity field, press Backspace; read the field.
Key 1, read the field; key 5, read the field. Click Add to Cart and open /cart; read the line and its quantity. Empty the cart.
On the book page select the whole quantity field, press Backspace, key 7; read the field.
cases.observe: the field after each key, the quantity of the cart line that results, and the field after the second erase and key 7

row.what: clear and re-key the quantity on the book page
row.behavior: the book page quantity field behaves as a person keys it
row.boundary: live stand: field and cart lines
row.completion: each keying done and the field and the line recorded

cases.title: Cart - keying 12 into the quantity field of a line
cases.given: A guest session. The book "1984" (stock 15 on the seed; read it on the book page first). Start quantities as parameters: 2, 1, 3, 5, 10.
steps: Put "1984" in the cart with the first start quantity (book page, quantity, Add to Cart); open /cart.
Click the line's quantity field, select the whole value, key 1 and then 2, one character at a time (never a paste); watch the requests the page sends after each key.
Read the field, the focus, and the line's quantity; reload /cart and read the line again.
Do the last three steps for each of the other start quantities (1, 3, 5, 10). Empty the cart.

thens.text: A number such as 12 can be keyed into the quantity field of a cart line: the field ends holding 12 and the line's quantity is 12, also after a reload, from every start quantity.
thens.ref: owner, gate A: Q3 a (a failure is a bug; a number such as 12 can be keyed), experiments/mybooks/cart-1-run-problems.md B-1; R-10

row.what: key 12 into the cart quantity field from several start quantities
row.behavior: a two-digit quantity can be keyed into a cart line
row.boundary: live stand: field, focus, requests, line quantity
row.completion: 12 keyed from each start and the line read after reload

cases.title: Cart - clearing the quantity field of a line
cases.given: A guest session. The book "1984".
steps: Put "1984" in the cart with quantity 2 (book page, quantity, Add to Cart); open /cart.
Click the line's quantity field, select the whole value, press Backspace; watch the request the page sends.
Read what the page shows (field, messages) and the line's quantity; reload /cart and read the quantity. Empty the cart.
cases.observe: the body of the request sent when the field is cleared, what the page shows, and the quantity after a reload

row.what: clear the quantity field of a cart line
row.behavior: clearing the cart quantity field is handled
row.boundary: live stand: request, page, line quantity
row.completion: the field cleared and the request, page and reload recorded

cases.title: Cart - the read of a book fails
cases.given: A guest session. Two books, "1984" and "Dune". The book read is the request GET /api/books/<id> (the cart page reads each line's book).
steps: Put "1984" and "Dune" in the cart (quantity 1 each) and leave the book pages.
fail_request the book read (glob */api/books/*) with status 500 from now on.
Open /cart; read what the page shows (look and read the lines and prices).
restore_request the book read; reload /cart and read the lines. Empty the cart.
cases.observe: what the cart page shows while the read of a book answers 500 (page text, lines, prices, any message)
teardown: restore_request */api/books/* (the book read answers as before).
Empty the cart.

row.what: book read fails while the cart page loads
scenarios: book read answers 500 on the cart page
row.behavior: the cart page under a failed book read
row.boundary: live stand: the cart page text
row.completion: the failure injected and the page recorded

cases.title: Cart - the cart read, a quantity change and a removal fail
cases.given: A guest session. Two books, "1984" and "Dune".
steps: Put "1984" and "Dune" in the cart (quantity 1 each).
fail_request the cart read (glob */api/cart) with status 500 from now on; open /cart; read what the page shows. restore_request.
fail_request the quantity change (glob */api/cart/*) with status 500; on /cart change a quantity; read the page and the line; restore_request.
fail_request the removal (glob */api/cart/*) with status 500; click remove on a line; read the page and the lines; restore_request. Empty the cart.
cases.observe: what the cart page shows in each of the three failures: the failed cart read, the failed quantity change, the failed removal
teardown: restore_request for every failure set in the steps.
Empty the cart.

row.what: cart read, quantity change and removal fail
row.behavior: the cart page under failed cart calls
row.boundary: live stand: the cart page text and lines
row.completion: each failure injected and the page recorded

cases.dropped: The card names PUT and DELETE separately; the recorder's fail_request takes one URL glob, so the change and the removal both use */api/cart/*.

cases.title: Catalog - a quick view of a book
cases.given: A guest session.
steps: Open the catalog, then a category, then the search; on each page hover the book cards.
Look for a quick-view control (an eye icon or the words Quick view) on a card.
Open a card and read whether it goes to the book page or to a quick view.

thens.text: A shopper can open a quick view of a book from the catalog and add the book to the cart from it.
thens.ref: Jira XPANBFLFA-160 (Add product from quick view)

row.what: add a product from a quick view
scenarios: find the quick view on the catalog, a category and the search
row.behavior: the catalog offers a quick view that adds to the cart
row.boundary: live stand: the catalog pages
row.completion: the three listing pages searched for a quick view

cases.title: Book page - the add is dropped by the network
cases.given: A guest session. The book "1984".
steps: Open the book page of "1984".
fail_request the add (glob */api/cart) with timeout from now on; click Add to Cart; read the message, the badge and whether the button works again.
restore_request the add; wait a few seconds without clicking; open /cart and read the lines (how many copies of "1984").

thens.text: When the add fails the page shows an error and recovers (the button works again) or tells the shopper to retry.
thens.ref: Jira TC-016

thens.text: After the network returns the system completes the action: the book is in the cart, exactly once, without a further click.
thens.ref: owner, gate A 02.11: Q8 a (the system completes the action after the network returns)

teardown: restore_request */api/cart (the add answers as before).
Empty the cart.

row.what: the add is dropped by the network
row.behavior: a dropped add is reported and completed
row.boundary: live stand: message, badge, cart lines
row.completion: the failure injected, restored, and the cart read

cases.dropped: Card step 'DevTools Offline' becomes fail_request with timeout (the vocabulary has no offline switch).

cases.title: Catalog - a book with stock 0
cases.given: A guest session. The book "Out of Print Classic" (stock 0 on the seed; read its stock on its page first).
steps: Open the catalog and find the card of "Out of Print Classic".
Read the state and the text of the card's Add button; try to click it; read any message and the badge.
Open /cart and read the lines.

thens.text: The card shows the book as out of stock to the shopper.
thens.ref: AC-2 Jira XPANBFLFA-44 (out of stock is shown); Jira 143

thens.text: A disabled Add button is enough: the book cannot be added, and the cart stays as it was.
thens.ref: owner, gate A 02.11: Q5 a (a disabled button is enough)

row.what: a book with stock 0 on the catalog card
row.behavior: a book with no stock cannot be added from the catalog
row.boundary: live stand: card state, text, cart lines
row.completion: the card read and the cart read

cases.dropped: Card step 'POST /api/cart with that bookId gives 400 OUT_OF_STOCK': no POST in the step vocabulary (F4).

cases.title: Book page - quantity above the stock and the maximum
cases.given: A guest session. The book "1984"; read its stock on its page first (N below).
steps: Open the book page of "1984".
Key 999 into the quantity field, click Add to Cart; read the message and /cart.
Key N+1, click Add to Cart; read the message and /cart.
Key N, click Add to Cart; read the message and /cart. Empty the cart.

thens.text: 999 and N+1 are each refused whole: a message says so and the cart stays as it was.
thens.ref: owner, gate A 02.11: Q2 a (refuse whole), Q3 a (maximum = stock)

thens.text: N is added: the cart line holds N.
thens.ref: Jira TC-010

row.what: quantity above the stock and 999
row.behavior: a quantity above the stock is refused whole; the stock itself is added
row.boundary: live stand: message and cart lines
row.completion: the three values keyed and the cart read

cases.title: Guest cart after registration and the first sign-in
cases.given: A guest session. The book "Dune". Limit of this run: no step of the recorder creates a new account (the new-account step is Slice 2). Walk up to the registration page, read the form, and give the Then `inconclusive` with the limitation "new-account step is Slice 2 (not in this recorder)".
steps: Put "Dune" in the cart with quantity 2 as a guest; read the badge.
Open /register and read the form (look); stop there.

thens.text: After the guest registers and signs in for the first time with the new account, the account cart holds "Dune" x2 (the guest cart is carried over).
thens.ref: owner, gate A 31.10: Q2 a (in scope); R-4 states the carry-over

teardown: Empty the cart.

row.what: guest cart after registration and first sign-in
row.behavior: the guest cart is carried into a new account
row.boundary: live stand: badge and the registration form
row.completion: the walk reaches /register and says what it could not do

cases.dropped: Registration and the first sign-in cannot be driven (F4, card 21 per sec 2): the case ends inconclusive by design.

cases.title: Cart - multi-digit keying and the badge and totals
cases.given: A guest session. The book "1984".
steps: Put "1984" in the cart with quantity 1; read the badge, the line's subtotal and the cart total.
On /cart key 1 then 2 into the line's quantity field, one character at a time; without reloading read the badge, the subtotal and the total.
Reload /cart and read the badge, the subtotal and the total. Empty the cart.

thens.text: A multi-digit quantity such as 12 can be keyed into a cart line and is kept.
thens.ref: Jira XPANBFLFA-200

thens.text: The badge, the line subtotal and the cart total show the new numbers right after the change, without a reload (badge = sum of quantities, total = sum of price x quantity).
thens.ref: Jira XPANBFLFA-201

row.what: multi-digit keying and the badge and totals
row.behavior: a multi-digit change updates the badge and the totals
row.boundary: live stand: field, badge, subtotal, total
row.completion: 12 keyed and the numbers read before and after a reload

cases.dropped: Card 23 has no steps-by-hand field; the steps are the multi-digit keying of card 3 and the read of badge, subtotal and total named by the two Jira bugs (R-11).

steps: Put "1984" in the wishlist (the wishlist control on its page or card); open the wishlist and read it.
fail_request the wishlist removal (glob */api/wishlist/*) with status 500 from now on.
Click Move to cart on "1984"; read the message and the wishlist; open /cart and read the lines; reload the wishlist and read it.
restore_request the wishlist removal.
cases.observe: the message shown after Move to cart, what the wishlist holds and what the cart holds, before and after a reload
teardown: restore_request */api/wishlist/* (the removal answers as before).

row.what: Move to cart while the wishlist removal fails
scenarios: wishlist removal answers 500 on Move to cart
row.behavior: Move to cart under a failed removal
row.boundary: live stand: message, wishlist, cart

cases.title: Wishlist - the network drops an add, a removal or the read
cases.given: The signed-in user. The book "1984".
steps: Put "1984" in the wishlist; open the wishlist.
fail_request the cart add (glob */api/cart) with timeout; click Move to cart; read the page and the wishlist; restore_request.
fail_request the wishlist removal (glob */api/wishlist/*) with timeout; click Remove; read the page and the wishlist; restore_request.
fail_request the wishlist read (glob */api/wishlist) with status 500, reload the wishlist and read the page; restore_request, reload and read the page.
cases.observe: what the page shows after each of the three failures: Move to cart, Remove and the wishlist read
teardown: restore_request for every failure set in the steps.

row.what: the network drops a wishlist add, removal or read
row.behavior: the wishlist page under dropped calls
row.boundary: live stand: the wishlist page text
row.completion: each failure injected and the page recorded

cases.title: Sign-in - the merge of the guest cart fails
cases.given: The seed user (the account cart empty: sign in, open /cart, remove every line, sign out first). The book "Dune".
steps: Make sure you are signed out. As a guest put "Dune" in the cart with quantity 2.
fail_request the merge (glob */api/cart/merge) with status 500 from now on. {LOGIN:user} Read the page, any message, and the cart; sign out; restore_request.
As a guest put "Dune" in the cart with quantity 2 again. fail_request the merge with timeout from now on. {LOGIN:user} Read the page, any message, and the cart; restore_request.

thens.text: When the merge answers 500 the shopper is told in words that the guest cart could not be carried over (or the guest items are not lost silently); a signed-in page with an empty cart and no word is not acceptable.
thens.ref: owner, gate A 05.11: Q13 a (say it in words); R-12

thens.text: When the merge gets no answer the shopper is told in words and is not left on the sign-in form with no word.
thens.ref: owner, gate A 05.11: Q13 a (say it in words); R-12

teardown: restore_request */api/cart/merge (the merge answers as before).
Signed in, remove every line of the cart.

row.what: the merge of the guest cart fails at sign-in
row.behavior: a failed merge is told in words
row.boundary: live stand: page, message, cart
row.completion: both failures injected and the page and cart recorded

cases.title: Sign-in - the merge keeps the higher quantity
cases.given: The seed user and the book "1984" (stock 15).
steps: Signed in, put "1984" in the account cart with quantity 1; sign out.
As a guest put "1984" in the cart with quantity 3; {LOGIN:user} Open /cart and read the line of "1984".
Remove the line; sign out. Signed in again put "1984" with quantity 3 in the account cart; sign out. As a guest put "1984" with quantity 2 in the cart; {LOGIN:user} Open /cart and read the line.

thens.text: Guest 3 and account 1 give one line of "1984" with quantity 3 (the higher quantity wins, not the sum 4).
thens.ref: MyBooks/docs/AUTH.md:8 (higher quantity wins)

thens.text: Guest 2 and account 3 give one line of "1984" with quantity 3.
thens.ref: MyBooks/docs/AUTH.md:8 (higher quantity wins)

teardown: Signed in, remove every line of the cart.

row.what: the merge keeps the higher quantity
row.behavior: the merge keeps the higher quantity of the same book
row.boundary: live stand: the cart lines after sign-in
row.completion: both pairs merged and the line read

cases.title: Add after the session ends
cases.given: The seed user and the book "1984". Limit of this run: no step of the recorder deletes a session cookie. Walk up to the point and give the Then `inconclusive` with the limitation "no step can delete a session cookie".
steps: Open the book page of "1984"; read the header (who is signed in) and the Add to Cart button.
Stop before the add: the session cannot be ended by any step.

thens.text: When the session has ended, adding a book asks the shopper to sign in (or extends the session) and the product is added only after that; the book is not added to a guest cart while the header still shows a signed-in user.
thens.ref: Jira TC-017; owner, gate A 02.11: Q9 b (require sign-in)

row.what: add after the session ends
row.behavior: an add after a session end asks for sign-in
row.boundary: live stand: header and book page
row.completion: the walk reaches the point and says what it could not do

cases.dropped: Card steps 2-4 (delete the session cookie, press Add, read GET /api/auth/session and GET /api/cart): no step deletes a cookie (F4); the case ends inconclusive by design.

cases.title: Two browsers on one cart - an edit after a removal elsewhere
cases.given: The seed user in two browsers: the first actor `user`, the second actor the same user by `--as env:USER_EMAIL/USER_PASSWORD` (the names of the variables, never values). The books "1984" and "Dune".
steps: In the first browser put "1984" and "Dune" in the cart (quantity 1 each); open /cart and leave it open.
In the second browser (second actor) sign in, open /cart and remove the line of "1984"; read /cart.
In the first browser (without reloading) change the quantity of "1984" to 2; read the page; open /api/cart in the first browser and read what the server holds.

thens.text: After the edit the first browser's cart page shows exactly the lines and quantities the server holds (the cart equals the server state); the line removed in the second browser is not shown as present.
thens.ref: Jira XPANBFLFA-174

teardown: Empty the cart (any browser).

row.what: an edit in a stale browser after a removal in another
row.behavior: the page equals the server cart after a stale edit
row.boundary: live stand: cart page and GET /api/cart
row.completion: both browsers acted and the page compared to the server

cases.dropped: Card 'two tabs of /cart' becomes two browsers (second actor, --as): the owner's reading of the card.

read the badge in browser one

thens.ref: owner 05.11 about 21:10: trimming the merged line to the stock is right

teardown: As admin set the stock of "Ariel" back to the number read first; read it back.

cases.title: Never-run cart rules - a guest line out of stock, stock fallen, the last copy in two carts
cases.given: Start signed out, as a guest. Two actors: `user` (the seed user) and `admin` (the second actor, `--as admin`; for the last-copy rule admin also shops as a second customer). Books "Moby-Dick" (stock 4), "Ariel" (stock 5) and "Last Copy" (stock 1); read each stock first and keep it: the teardown puts it back. The test card for the checkout is 4242424242424242. This case changes data of the stand.
steps: As a guest put "Moby-Dick" in the cart (quantity 1). As the second actor (admin) set the stock of "Moby-Dick" to 0. {LOGIN:user} Open /cart and read the lines and the badge.

As the user put "Ariel" in the cart with quantity 4. As admin set the stock of "Ariel" to 2. As the user open /cart and read the line; proceed to checkout and place the order with the test card; read the answer. Then set the quantity of "Ariel" to 2 in the cart and read the answer.

As the user put "Last Copy" in the cart (quantity 1); as the second actor (admin, shopping) put "Last Copy" in its cart (quantity 1). As the user place the order; then as the second actor place the order; read both answers.

thens.text: At sign-in the guest line of "Moby-Dick" (stock now 0) is dropped: it is not in the cart, the badge is absent or 0.
thens.ref: add-to-cart-cases.md AC-09

thens.text: With the stock of "Ariel" fallen to 2 the cart keeps the line x4; the order is refused ("Insufficient stock" for Ariel), no order is created, the stock stays 2; after the quantity is set to 2 it is accepted.
thens.ref: add-to-cart-cases.md AC-11

thens.text: The first order for "Last Copy" is created (stock becomes 0); the second is refused for insufficient stock and no order is created for it.
thens.ref: add-to-cart-cases.md AC-12

teardown: As admin set the stock of "Moby-Dick", "Ariel" and "Last Copy" back to the numbers read first; read each back.
Remove every line of the user's and of admin's cart.

row.what: never-run cart rules (AC-09, AC-11, AC-12)
scenarios: guest line out of stock at sign-in
row.behavior: the cart and checkout keep stock rules
row.boundary: live stand: cart lines, checkout answers
row.completion: the three rules walked and the stocks restored

cases.dropped: AC-13 (a book deleted while it is in a cart) stays out: it needs a book deleted. AC-11 steps 5 (cart empty after a successful order) not walked: it needs an order that succeeds.
